metrics.justification: Responded to a run of communal flashpoints: condemned the slapping of a non-Muslim man for eating during Ramadan (17 Mar 2025) and referred it to police, and on an upside-down national-flag episode (Aug 2025) urged firm action then walked it back to "most likely unintentional." Prompt public handling, but enforcement sat with police and the flag reversal looked reactive (anchor 2).

citation.title: Cops to probe slapping incident, says Unity Minister

metrics.justification: Told Parliament (29 Jul 2025) that existing laws were sufficient and no new harmony statute was needed, then by 7 Apr 2026 said the government would revisit drafting a National Harmony and Reconciliation Commission bill; meanwhile the ministry built administrative tools (the eSepakat reporting system, a unity dashboard). The long-promised harmony legislation was not delivered, administrative mechanisms aside (anchor 2).

citation.title: Putrajaya to revisit proposed national harmony bill, says Aaron

metrics.justification: Articulated a whole-of-government approach to race-religion-royalty issues through an inter-ministerial Unity Issues Management Committee coordinating 12 ministries and agencies, splitting enforcement from mediation. A documented coordinating instrument, but no cross-bench or independent statutory body stood up (anchor 2).

citation.title: Govt takes 'whole of government' approach to 3R issues, says Aaron

metrics.justification: Reversed his stance on harmony legislation, from "no need for new laws" (29 Jul 2025) to reviving the harmony-commission bill (7 Apr 2026), giving rising communal tensions as the reason; but the reporting shows him explaining the new direction rather than explicitly owning the earlier position as a reversal (anchor 2).
